183	## 4. Special states that need extra care
184	
185	- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
186	- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.
203

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |

content.content:
# Error taxonomy — 13 codes

Every endpoint returns errors as `{ code, message, retryable }`. The list below is closed: no other code exists.

| Code | HTTP | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | 401 | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | 401 | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | _(no HTTP response — see note)_ | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | 502 | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | 504 | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | yes |
| `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` | 400 | no |
| `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | no |
| `OCR_NO_TEXT` | 400 | no |

**Two deliberate design choices (these never happen in this API):**
- **Never `403`** — a resource belonging to another user always answers `404 NOT_FOUND` (so its existence is not revealed).
- **Never `409`** — the idempotency of RF10 (re-sending the same chat message as an entry) always answers `200`; there is no "conflict" code.

**`NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP status:** it is the only code that never becomes an actual response — it represents a connection that ends without any response.
---known-bugs---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

content.content:
9:**Input**: User description: "P-F000 — Foundation: Build the foundation that every later unit uses (project scaffold, design tokens, HTTP client with Either/Failure error mapping, login/sign-up, splash, base navigation, expired-session overlay), as described in docs/input/requirements.md section 12, without implementing RF01–RF10, hardcoding visual values outside design_tokens.dart, or changing the backend."
23:1. **Given** a user with a valid existing account and no active session, **When** they enter the correct email and password on the login screen and submit, **Then** they are authenticated and taken to the Home/Chat screen.
33:**Why this priority**: Required for anyone without an account to enter the product at all, but it depends on the same screen and session machinery as login, so it is one step below it.
44:### User Story 3 - App launches and routes by session state (Priority: P3)
46:Whenever the app is opened, it shows a brief splash state, checks whether a usable session already exists, and sends the user straight to Home/Chat or to the login/sign-up screen accordingly — without ever leaving them stuck on the splash screen.
48:**Why this priority**: Determines where every single app session begins; it depends on User Story 1 existing but is a thin routing layer on top of it rather than new user-facing capability.
50:**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by launching the app under three stored-session conditions (valid, expired-but-refreshable, none) and confirming the correct landing screen each time.
54:1. **Given** a device with a previously stored, still-valid session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands directly on Home/Chat without re-entering credentials.
55:2. **Given** a device with no stored session (first launch, or after logout), **When** the app is launched, **Then** after the splash state the user lands on the login/sign-up screen.
56:3. **Given** a device with an expired-but-refreshable session, **When** the app is launched, **Then** the app renews the session in the background and lands on Home/Chat without prompting the user.
72:3. **Given** the user is on any main screen, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** the menu overlays the current screen without discarding the state underneath it.
76:### User Story 5 - Session expires during active use (Priority: P5)
78:While the user is actively on a screen (e.g., scrolled partway through Home/Chat), the backend session expires; an overlay appears explaining this and offering to log in again, and once they do, they return to exactly where they were.
80:**Why this priority**: An edge condition of an already-working session (Story 1); important for trust and data safety, but it cannot be exercised until login and at least one screen exist.
82:**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a session-expired response while a screen is in a known state, confirming the overlay appears over it unchanged, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact state.
86:1. **Given** the user is actively viewing a screen in a particular state (e.g., a given scroll position), **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** a "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the current screen without resetting its state.
87:2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible, **When** the user taps "Entrar novamente" and re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay is dismissed and the underlying screen is restored exactly as it was.
95:- The stored access token is present but its refresh token is itself invalid or expired at launch — the user is routed to the login screen, never left stuck on the splash state.
96:- The session expires a second time while the user is still dismissing a "Sessão expirada" overlay from the first expiration — the overlay persists/reappears rather than letting the user proceed with a stale session.
98:- The app is backgrounded mid-submission of login or sign-up — on resume, the request either completes normally or fails cleanly, and never results in a duplicate account or a duplicate session.
112:- **FR-009**: The system MUST check, on every app launch, whether a usable session already exists — renewing it first if it is merely expired-but-renewable — and route the user to Home/Chat when one exists or to the login screen otherwise.
113:- **FR-010**: The system MUST show a splash state while this session check (and any related background preparation) is in progress, before routing the user anywhere.
116:- **FR-013**: The system MUST show a "Sessão expirada" overlay on top of whatever screen the user is on when the backend reports the session has expired, without discarding that screen's state underneath.
117:- **FR-014**: Users MUST be able to dismiss the "Sessão expirada" overlay by re-authenticating, after which the screen underneath MUST be restored to its prior state.
118:- **FR-015**: The system MUST present a clear, non-crashing message for every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, or session-check can return.
124:- **Session**: Represents whether the user is currently authenticated — holds the information needed to stay logged in and to know when it has expired or can be silently renewed. Determines whether a launch routes to Home/Chat or to the login screen, and whether an active screen receives the "Sessão expirada" overlay.
126:- **Backend Failure**: The error outcome every call introduced by this unit (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can produce — carries enough information to distinguish a retryable problem from a non-retryable one, and to choose the message shown to the user.
133:- **SC-001**: 100% of returning users with a valid stored session reach Home/Chat automatically after the splash state, with no login step required.
135:- **SC-003**: Every error condition that sign-up, login, session-renewal, and session-check can return produces a readable on-screen message rather than a blank screen, a crash, or an indefinite loading state.
137:- **SC-005**: When a session expires while a screen is in a particular state, that same state (e.g., scroll position, visible content) is unchanged after the user re-authenticates, in every observed case.
143:- Re-authenticating from the "Sessão expirada" overlay goes to the login screen (not to a biometric step), for the same reason — RF03 is not yet part of the app.
145:- Session renewal is attempted silently in the background whenever a request fails because the session has merely expired; the "Sessão expirada" overlay is shown only once silent renewal itself is not possible.
148:- Every error this unit's calls (sign-up, login, refresh, session check) can return is one of the backend's fixed, documented error codes; no other error shape is expected from these calls.

# Feature Specification: P-RF01 — Multimodal capture

**Feature Branch**: `003-multimodal-capture` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-12

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF01 — Multimodal capture: Let the user create a journal entry by text, audio recording or photo, from the Insertion Modal, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF01) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: Insertion modal — 'Texto', 'Áudio — Gravando', 'Foto — Captura' (prototype extract, section 2.3), opened by the '+' button of Home/Chat. Backend: POST /entries with source manual/audio/photo. Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

# Seeded entries for semantic search

Three journal entries present in the seed data of the backend environments. Each text deliberately avoids the root of the word searched for — the search can only find it by semantic similarity of the embedding, never by lexical coincidence (RF06). The texts are user content, in Portuguese, reproduced literally.

## Entry 1 — search term: `ansiedade`

> Amanhã tenho que apresentar o projeto pra diretoria inteira e não consigo
> parar de pensar nisso. O coração fica acelerado só de imaginar todo mundo
> olhando pra mim esperando eu falar. Passei a noite revisando os slides de
> novo e de novo, mas por dentro sinto um aperto no peito, as mãos ficam
> geladas e suando ao mesmo tempo. Tentei dormir mais cedo mas fiquei rodando
> os mesmos pensamentos, imaginando tudo que pode dar errado. Só queria que já
> fosse depois de amanhã pra essa sensação passar.

## Entry 2 — search term: `cansaço`

> Cheguei em casa hoje e simplesmente desabei no sofá sem forças pra fazer
> mais nada. A semana foi daquelas que parecem não ter fim, um dia emendando
> no outro sem espaço pra respirar. Meu corpo pesa, os olhos ardem, e até
> pensar em levantar pra tomar um banho parece um esforço enorme. Só quero
> ficar aqui parado, sem estímulo nenhum, até o corpo se recuperar um pouco.

## Entry 3 — search term: `gratidão`

> Hoje resolvi parar um minuto antes de dormir pra pensar no que rolou de bom
> no meu dia. Tive uma conversa gostosa com um amigo que eu não via há
> tempos, o café da manhã veio na hora certa bem quentinho, e ainda consegui
> resolver uma pendência que tava me incomodando. São coisas pequenas, mas
> quando junto tudo isso percebo que o dia não foi tão ruim assim. Fico
> pensando em como é bom ter essas pausas pra notar o que realmente importa.

# Feature Specification: P-RF01 — Multimodal capture

**Feature Branch**: `003-multimodal-capture` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-12

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF01 — Multimodal capture: Let the user create a journal entry by text, audio recording or photo, from the Insertion Modal, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF01) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: Insertion modal — 'Texto', 'Áudio — Gravando', 'Foto — Captura' (prototype extract, section 2.3), opened by the '+' button of Home/Chat. Backend: POST /entries with source manual/audio/photo. Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-12

- Q: When a user stops recording audio or captures a photo in this unit, how should Save behave, given RF02 (speech-to-text/OCR) is an explicitly later unit and the prototype states listed for this unit stop at "Gravando" and "Captura"? → A: RF01 performs the minimal on-device transcription (audio) or backend OCR call (photo) needed to produce text content inline, as part of confirming Save, shown with only a plain/generic loading indicator — not RF02's dedicated "Processando / Transcrito / Reconhecido / Erro" screens, their editable-text review step, or their specific retry affordances ("Tentar novamente", "Salvar só a foto"). This is the only reading under which RF01 alone satisfies its own stated acceptance criterion that all three modalities "result in the same persisted-entry format," since entries are immutable (no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`) and therefore cannot be corrected after creation — recognition must happen before the entry exists. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
- Q: After a successful Save, the modal closes back to Home/Chat — but Home/Chat never renders journal entries (those appear only in the later "Meus Registros" unit, RF07). What should FR-011's "reflected in the app's state" actually look like on Home/Chat itself? → A: Nothing new is shown on Home/Chat. The prototype documents no confirmation screen, toast, or any other on-screen change for this flow, and inventing one would conflict with Principle IV's visual-fidelity constraint (faithfulness to a frozen prototype that defines no such state) as well as SC-003's "no required intermediate screens." "Reflected in the app's state" means only that the newly created entry is added to the app's local entries store/cache — the same store later units (e.g., RF07) will read from — not that Home/Chat's UI changes in any visible way. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principles I and IV, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)
- Q: The backend's `POST /media/ocr` response carries a `confidence: "high"|"low"` field alongside the recognized text — does a `low`-confidence recognition get treated any differently from `high`-confidence before Save completes? → A: No. This unit's scope (FR-007) stops at automatically producing recognized text before Save; any quality gating, warning, or review step keyed to confidence is exactly the kind of recognition-quality handling RF02 owns (its "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" review states, deliberately deferred here). Confidence is therefore ignored in this unit: any non-empty recognized text, regardless of confidence, proceeds to Save normally; only the already-specified zero-usable-text case (Edge Cases) is treated as a failure. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where the input docs are silent on this exact boundary.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Writing a journal entry as text (Priority: P1)

A user wants to quickly note something in words. They tap "+" on Home/Chat, the Insertion Modal opens on its "Texto" tab, they write freely in the text field, and tap "Salvar". The modal closes and the note now exists as one of their journal entries.

**Why this priority**: The simplest and fully self-contained of the three capture paths — it has no dependency on recognition of any kind, so it is the first thing that must work end to end.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "+", typing text into the Texto tab, tapping "Salvar", and confirming a new entry with that exact text and origin "manual" now exists, and the modal has closed back to Home/Chat.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Home/Chat is open, **When** the user taps "+", **Then** the Insertion Modal opens as an overlay on top of Home/Chat (which stays in place underneath), defaulted to the "Texto" tab with an empty field.
2. **Given** the Texto tab with text typed into the field, **When** the user taps "Salvar", **Then** a new journal entry is created with that text as its content and origin "manual", and the modal closes, returning to Home/Chat.
3. **Given** the Texto tab with an empty field, **When** the user looks at "Salvar", **Then** the action is unavailable (disabled), so an empty entry can never be created.

---

### User Story 2 - Recording a journal entry as audio (Priority: P1)

A user prefers to speak rather than type. They tap "+", switch to the "Áudio" tab, tap the round start control, and recording begins with a visible waveform and timer. They tap stop, and after a brief moment the spoken content is saved as a journal entry just like a written one.

**Why this priority**: Voice capture is one of the two microphone/camera-dependent paths and, together with Story 1, establishes that every modality converges on the same entry format — the central acceptance criterion of this unit.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Áudio tab, recording a short spoken note, stopping the recording, confirming Save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "audio" and text content derived from what was spoken.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Áudio" tab, **Then** it shows an idle state with a round start control and the caption "Toque para gravar", with no recording yet; **When** the user taps that control, **Then** recording starts, showing a stop control, an animated waveform, and a running mm:ss timer.
2. **Given** an active recording, **When** the user taps stop, **Then** the recording ends and the system automatically transcribes it and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "audio" and the transcribed text as its content.
3. **Given** a completed audio capture that is being transcribed and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
4. **Given** transcription or the save itself fails (e.g., inaudible recording, network timeout), **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to re-record, as long as the captured audio is still held locally.

---

### User Story 3 - Capturing a journal entry from a photo (Priority: P2)

A user has something written down on paper, a receipt, or a whiteboard. They tap "+", switch to the "Foto" tab, choose "Câmera" or "Galeria", and the text in the image becomes a journal entry.

**Why this priority**: Mirrors Story 2's recognition pipeline for a second input type; ordered after audio because the text-recognition concern it shares with Story 2 is already established there.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the Foto tab, choosing "Câmera" or "Galeria" to supply an image containing legible text, confirming the save completes, and confirming a new entry exists with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the Insertion Modal is open, **When** the user switches to the "Foto" tab, **Then** two options are shown — "Câmera" and "Galeria" — with no image selected yet.
2. **Given** the user picks "Câmera" or "Galeria" and supplies an image, **When** that image is provided, **Then** the system automatically extracts its text and completes the save as part of confirming the capture, producing one new entry with origin "photo" and the recognized text as its content.
3. **Given** a completed photo capture that is being recognized and saved, **When** that processing is underway, **Then** the user sees a plain loading indicator (not a detailed multi-state screen) until it finishes.
4. **Given** text recognition or the save itself fails, **When** that happens, **Then** no entry is created, a clear failure message is shown, and the user can retry without having to recapture the image, as long as it is still held locally.

---

### User Story 4 - Abandoning a capture leaves nothing behind (Priority: P3)

A user starts writing, recording, or photographing, changes their mind, and backs out. Nothing about that attempt is saved anywhere.

**Why this priority**: A safety property that applies across all three modalities rather than a feature of its own; depends on Stories 1–3 already existing to have something to abandon.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by starting each modality (typing a partial note, starting a recording, opening the camera/gallery picker) and closing the modal or navigating away before tapping Salvar, then confirming no new entry was created in any case.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** partially typed text in the Texto tab, **When** the user closes the modal without tapping "Salvar", **Then** no entry is created and the draft text is discarded.
2. **Given** an in-progress audio recording, **When** the user closes the modal or stops without confirming save, **Then** no entry is created and no partially-recorded audio is persisted as an entry.
3. **Given** the Foto tab's camera/gallery picker is open, **When** the user cancels it without completing a capture, **Then** no entry is created.

---

### Edge Cases

- Microphone or camera permission is denied at the OS level: the respective tab shows an explanatory message in place of the recording/capture controls, instead of silently failing or crashing.
- The user switches tabs while a recording is in progress: the in-progress recording is discarded (same outcome as closing the modal), since no partial entry may survive regardless of which tab is active afterward.
- The app is backgrounded or killed while a capture is in progress and unsaved, **or while it is stopped/captured and awaiting retry after a recognition or save failure**: nothing is lost that mattered, because nothing was persisted yet — the captured audio/image and any pending retry state exist only in memory for the current app session. On return (after a mere backgrounding, the modal resumes normally; after a kill, the modal reopens to its default empty state), and if the content was lost to a process kill, the user must recapture rather than retry.
- Transcription or OCR succeeds technically but returns no usable text (e.g., silence, a blank or illegible image): Save fails with a clear message rather than creating an empty or near-empty entry. A `low`-confidence OCR result that still contains text is not treated as a failure — confidence-based quality gating is out of scope for this unit (reserved for RF02) — so Save proceeds normally with whatever text was recognized.
- The device is offline when the user taps "Salvar": the save is blocked immediately with a clear message, without attempting a network call that cannot succeed, consistent with this product's cloud-only architecture (no offline writes).
- The user double-taps "Salvar": only one entry is ever created per confirmed capture, never duplicates.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

# Cerne Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Product Source of Truth
`docs/input/` — `requirements.md`, `prototype/`, and `backend/` — is the
authoritative source for product behavior. `requirements.md` defines
functional and quality requirements, screens, the API surface, delivery
order, and technical constraints; `prototype/` is the frozen visual
reference and its token/state extract; `backend/` documents the existing
API, error taxonomy, screen-state map, sync-badge semantics, and fixtures.
Where these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable
technical decision rather than block on clarification. Files under
`docs/input/` are frozen inputs and MUST NOT be edited by anyone working in
this repository.

Rationale: a reflective-journaling app with a frozen, already-documented
backend has exactly one place where ambiguity should be resolved — the
product input — so decisions stay traceable and the backend contract stays
stable.

### II. Fixed Technology Stack
The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention

The app is built with Flutter and Dart at the version pinned via `fvm`,
using `flutter_bloc` for state management and Clean Architecture with three
layers per feature. Error handling MUST use `fpdart`, with every repository
returning `Either<Failure, T>`. Test doubles MUST use `mocktail`. Speech-to-
text runs on-device via `whisper_ggml`; audio content MUST NEVER be sent to
the backend. The shipping platform is iOS. Choices not fixed here — routing,
HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics,
and charting — are open implementation decisions.

Rationale: a single, non-negotiable stack removes a whole category of
architectural debate and keeps the codebase consistent across features
built by different contributors or at different times.

### III. Backend Boundary — Frozen Backend, No Direct AI Calls
The backend is already built and frozen. The app consumes it strictly as
documented in `docs/input/backend/`, including its API contract
(`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`); the app MUST NOT change the
backend, its API contract, or its configuration. All AI features, including
semantic search, are provided exclusively by the backend — the app MUST
NEVER call an AI provider directly. Configuration and credentials come from
a project-root `.env` with exactly two variables: `FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL` and
`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Every call to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` MUST
carry the header `apikey: <SUPABASE_ANON_KEY>`. The `Authorization: Bearer`
header carries `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` for operations that need no user session
(sign-up, login, refresh) and the user's access token for every operation
marked `bearerAuth` in the OpenAPI contract. `.env` and any credential MUST
NEVER be committed.

Rationale: the backend and its AI integrations are out of this project's
scope and already relied upon elsewhere; treating them as an immutable,
narrowly-accessed contract prevents scope creep and accidental coupling or
credential leakage.

### IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity
`lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography,
spacing, and radii. No visual value MAY be hardcoded anywhere else. The UI
MUST be faithful to `docs/input/prototype/`. UI text MUST be in Portuguese,
exactly as written in the prototype; code identifiers, comments, and project
documentation MUST be in English.

Rationale: a single token source makes visual fidelity (RNF08) mechanically
checkable, and separating UI language (Portuguese, matching the frozen
prototype) from code language (English) keeps the codebase reviewable while
preserving the product's voice.

### V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention
Code MUST follow the folder convention:
```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/

# Cerne — Prototype extract

The visual reference of the product is `cerne-prototype.html` (this folder). Open it in a browser; it needs JavaScript. This extract lists its navigable states, its visual tokens, its components and the implementation notes that come with it.

- **Frame:** 390 × 844 logical points, portrait only, 4 dp grid.
- **Language of the interface:** Portuguese. Every UI text below appears exactly as in the prototype, in quotes.
- **Precedence:** the prototype defines appearance and states. Behavior rules (triggers, timings, filters, error handling) are defined in `docs/input/requirements.md`; where the prototype's simulated behavior differs from a requirement, the requirement prevails.

---

## 1. Navigation map

The prototype has **32 navigable states**, reachable from a single state machine (a `screen` variable plus overlay flags). Not every state is a new full screen — several are **overlays** (modal, sheet, bottom sheet, dialog) shown on top of one of three base screens: **Home/Chat**, **Meus Registros** and **Configurações**. Overlays preserve the screen underneath (it stays visible, with a darkened scrim behind).

```
Splash (auto, 1.8 s)
  └─> Biometria ──tap/error──> PIN inicial / PIN após falha
  │      └─> "usar e-mail e senha" ──> Entrar / criar conta (toggle)
  │                                          └─> submit ──> Home/Chat
  └─(PIN complete, 4 digits)──> Home/Chat
  └─(Face ID/Touch ID ok)──> Home/Chat

Home/Chat (base screen)
  ├─ overlay: Sessão expirada (backend session expires; "Entrar novamente" ──> Biometria)
  ├─ overlay: side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation
  └─ overlay: Insertion modal ("+" button) ──> tabs Texto / Áudio / Foto, each with its own sub-states
        (on save, the modal closes and returns to Home/Chat with the record added)

Meus Registros (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period

Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)

Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
  ├─ inline profile-name editing
  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
```

---

## 2. Navigable states

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
---rf02 spec FR excerpt---
108:- The device is offline when OCR would normally be attempted: "Foto — Processando OCR" MUST resolve to "Foto — Erro" with a clear, offline-appropriate message (not a generic failure) rather than hanging; "Salvar só a foto" and "Tentar novamente" remain visible, but "Salvar" (from a would-be "Reconhecido" state) and "Salvar só a foto" both still require connectivity for the underlying `POST /entries` call, following the same offline-blocks-writes rule established in RF01.

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).
- **FR-002**: Entries MUST be grouped under date headings by the calendar day they occurred ("Hoje" for today, "Ontem" for yesterday, an explicit date for anything older), with each entry rendered as a card showing: a marker and icon distinguishing its origin, its time, a text excerpt, any attached tags as read-only chips (only when present), and a per-entry synchronization badge.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST support browsing the user's complete entry history beyond what fits in a single fetch, loading further entries automatically as the user scrolls, and appending them without disturbing already-rendered cards or the user's current scroll position.
- **FR-004**: When the signed-in user has zero entries, the screen MUST show an empty state (illustration, "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action) instead of an empty list; completing a save from that action MUST return the user to this screen with the new entry visible in its correct date group.
- **FR-005**: The per-entry synchronization badge MUST independently reflect exactly one of three states — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed for each entry from its own server-confirmed data together with the device's own knowledge of any write still pending or unreconciled for that entry, following the sync-badge semantics; this computation and its on-screen state MUST NOT depend on, be blocked by, or be delayed by session or authentication handling (login, silent renewal, or the expired-session overlay).
- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.
- **FR-007**: If the session cannot be silently renewed while this screen is open, the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay MUST appear on top of it without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position; once the user re-authenticates, the overlay MUST dismiss and the screen MUST be restored exactly as it was. - **FR-008**: The screen's header download affordance and its search bar with funnel button MUST be rendered to match the prototype for visual fidelity, but MUST NOT perform export or search/filter behavior in this unit — those behaviors belong to later units and MUST NOT be implemented here.
- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.

- **Journal Entry**: The same persisted, immutable record introduced by RF01 — text content, a creation/occurrence time, and an origin — now also carrying the server-confirmation data (its last-confirmed-write time and the ever-increasing revision counter) and any read-only tags attached to it, and now rendered regardless of which of the four possible origins (`manual`, `audio`, `photo`, `chat`) produced it.
- **Synchronization Badge State**: A derived, per-entry value — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed entirely on the device from an entry's own confirmation data and the device's own record of any write for that entry still pending or unreconciled; never itself stored by or requested directly from the backend.
- **Entry Timeline Page**: The windowed view of the user's full entry history currently loaded on screen — the entries fetched so far and the position to continue from — preserved across scrolling, backgrounding, and a session expiration/renewal cycle so the user's place is never lost.

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of a user's entries — across every origin they've used — appear exactly once in the timeline, correctly grouped by the day they occurred, with no entry requiring the user to know or remember which capture method created it.
- **SC-002**: 100% of accounts with zero entries see the empty state with a working path into creating their first entry, never a blank, broken, or perpetually-loading screen.
- **SC-003**: Users can scroll through their entire entry history, however long, with additional entries loading automatically in every case, without ever needing a manual "load more" action or losing their scroll position.
- **SC-004**: When a session expires while a user is viewing this screen, 100% of the time their loaded entries and scroll position are unchanged after they re-authenticate.
- **SC-005**: Every entry visible on screen shows one of the three defined synchronization states at all times, unaffected by whatever is happening with the user's session at that moment.

## Assumptions

- The header's download icon and the search bar with its funnel button are rendered to match the prototype (visual fidelity) but are inert placeholders in this unit; their behavior belongs to RF05 (export) and RF06 (search/filter), both later in the delivery order.
- No entry can currently be created with origin `chat` (RF04's chat and RF10's "save to journal" are later units), but because `GET /entries` is origin-agnostic and the prototype's component library already defines a visual treatment for all four origins, this screen renders `chat`-origin entries correctly if the backend ever returns one (e.g., from seed data) rather than treating it as an error case.
- This unit introduces no new local database. It reuses the in-memory entries store RF01 already created and documented as available for later units to read, merging it with the entries this screen fetches and paginates from the backend.
- The "synchronizing" and "synchronization error" badge states are implemented completely and correctly per `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`, and must respond correctly to whatever pending or failed local write state exists for an entry. Because RF01's existing save flow only ever makes an entry visible anywhere after the backend has already confirmed it, these two states may rarely or never be observed through today's own capture flow alone — that does not make their correct implementation optional, since the requirement's acceptance criterion is about the badge's independence from the authentication stream, not about how often each state is exercised by this unit's own flows.
- Date-heading grouping ("Hoje", "Ontem", explicit dates) uses the device's local calendar day applied to each entry's occurrence timestamp, matching the prototype's labels.
- No entry-detail or full-text screen is introduced in this unit — see the resolved Clarification on `GET /entries/:id`'s purpose; a card's text excerpt is the only rendering of an entry's content here.
- "No BLoC imports another BLoC directly" (the requirement's own architecture-level acceptance criterion) is carried forward as an implementation-time constraint for the planning phase; at the specification level it is expressed through FR-005's and FR-007's independence requirements between the synchronization badge and session/authentication handling.

# Feature Specification: P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)

**Feature Branch**: `005-multi-source-timeline` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline): Show all of the user's entries in a timeline, whatever their origin, with a per-entry synchronization badge, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF07) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros' (default) and 'Tela 4 — Vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.4); the 'Sessão expirada' overlay (section 4). Badge semantics: docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md. Backend: GET /entries, GET /entries/:id, GET /auth/session, POST /auth/refresh. Depends on F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: RF01 (already delivered) opens the Insertion Modal only from Home/Chat's "+" button and, on a successful save, always returns the user to Home/Chat. This unit adds a second entry point — the "Criar primeiro registro" action on this screen's empty state — so where should a save started from there return the user to, and must the newly created entry appear here immediately? → A: It returns to this screen (Meus Registros), not to Home/Chat, and the newly created entry appears immediately in its correct date group. The entire purpose of the empty-state action is to take the user from zero entries to seeing their first one; returning them to Home/Chat instead would leave the empty state looking unresolved even though the entry was created. This reuses the same in-memory entries store RF01 already appends to on a successful save (and that it documented as existing "for later units ... to read"), merged with whatever this screen has already loaded from the backend. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
- Q: `GET /entries/:id` is listed under this requirement, but no entry-detail or full-text screen appears anywhere in the prototype's navigation map or navigable-state catalog for "Meus Registros" — only a card with a truncated text excerpt. What is this endpoint actually for in this unit? → A: It is not used to open a detail view (none is drawn anywhere, and inventing one would conflict with this unit's visual-fidelity obligation to the frozen prototype). Instead, this unit uses it to re-confirm the state of one specific, already-loaded entry during reconciliation — for example, after the "Sessão expirada" overlay is dismissed and the session is renewed — rather than re-fetching the entire paginated list, which is what keeps already-rendered cards and the scroll position from being disturbed, in line with this requirement's own acceptance criterion about not losing scroll position. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Seeing every entry in one place, regardless of how it was created (Priority: P1)

A user who has written notes, recorded audio, and captured photos over several days opens "Meus Registros" from the side menu and sees all of those entries together, in a single timeline, grouped by the day they happened ("Hoje", "Ontem", then calendar dates), each one visually marked with where it came from.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the screen exists — a user's journal is split across capture methods, and without this unified view there is no way to look back at everything they've recorded.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding a user with entries of different origins across different days, opening "Meus Registros", and confirming every entry appears exactly once, grouped under the correct date heading, with an origin-appropriate visual marker on each.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user with entries created as text, audio, and photo on different days, **When** they open "Meus Registros", **Then** every one of those entries appears in the list, grouped under date headings ("Hoje" for today's entries, "Ontem" for yesterday's, an explicit date for anything older), each showing a time, an origin-colored marker and icon, a text excerpt, and a synchronization badge.
2. **Given** an entry that has tags attached (from existing account data), **When** its card is rendered, **Then** those tags appear as read-only chips on the card; **given** an entry with no tags, **When** its card is rendered, **Then** no tag chips appear for it.
3. **Given** the list of entries is longer than fits on screen, **When** the user scrolls down, **Then** older entries load automatically and are appended to the list without disturbing the entries already shown or losing the user's scroll position.

---

### User Story 2 - Starting from nothing (Priority: P1)

A brand-new user, or one who has not yet created any entry, opens "Meus Registros" and sees a clear empty state instead of a blank or broken screen, with a direct path to creating their first entry.

**Why this priority**: Equally fundamental to Story 1 — this screen must handle the zero-entries case correctly from day one, since it is the state every account starts in.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening "Meus Registros" on an account with zero entries, confirming the empty-state illustration, message, and call-to-action appear, and confirming that action leads to creating an entry that then populates the screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an account with no entries at all, **When** the user opens "Meus Registros", **Then** they see the empty state — a notebook illustration, the message "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action — instead of an empty list.
2. **Given** the empty state is showing, **When** the user taps "Criar primeiro registro", **Then** the existing entry-creation flow opens; **when** they complete a save, **Then** they return to "Meus Registros" and see that new entry now populating the list in place of the empty state.

---

### User Story 3 - The session expires while browsing (Priority: P2)

A user is scrolled partway through their history when their backend session expires. A clear prompt to log in again appears over the screen, and once they do, they land back exactly where they were — same entries loaded, same scroll position.

**Why this priority**: An edge condition of Story 1 that protects against data loss and disorientation; it cannot be exercised until the timeline itself exists, but it is important enough to this requirement's own acceptance criteria to rank above cosmetic concerns.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading the timeline, scrolling to a known position, forcing a session-expired response, confirming the overlay appears without resetting the list, and confirming re-authentication restores that exact scroll position and content.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is scrolled to a particular position in "Meus Registros", **When** the backend reports the session has expired, **Then** the "Sessão expirada" overlay appears on top of the screen without discarding the loaded entries or resetting the scroll position.
2. **Given** the overlay is visible, **When** the user re-authenticates successfully, **Then** the overlay dismisses and the screen is restored exactly as it was, without reloading or reordering the entries already on screen.

---

### User Story 4 - The synchronization badge tells the truth, even during session trouble (Priority: P3)

While a user is looking at their timeline — including while a session renewal is happening in the background, or while the "Sessão expirada" overlay is up — each entry's synchronization badge keeps showing an accurate state (synchronized, synchronizing, or sync error) and is never frozen, blanked, or delayed by whatever is happening with the session.

**Why this priority**: A correctness and trust property layered on top of Story 1's display rather than a feature of its own; it depends on the timeline and the session-expiry handling of Story 3 already existing.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by putting entries in each of the three badge states, forcing a session expiration and renewal in the background, and confirming every badge's state is unaffected by that session activity throughout.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** entries in each of the three synchronization states, **When** a session renewal happens silently in the background, **Then** every badge still reflects its correct, unchanged state throughout and after the renewal.
2. **Given** the "Sessão expirada" overlay is visible over the timeline, **When** the user inspects the cards underneath (e.g., once it is dismissed), **Then** every badge's state is exactly what it was before the overlay appeared, with no badge having changed, frozen, or disappeared because of the session event.

---

### Edge Cases

- The device is offline while viewing this screen: already-loaded entries remain visible and scrollable (per the product's offline behavior), but loading further pages fails with a clear, retryable message instead of hanging or crashing; no write of any kind happens from this screen.
- The backend returns an entry whose origin is `chat` — a source this app cannot yet produce (chat and "save to journal" are later units) but that `GET /entries` can still return (e.g., from seed/test data): the card renders with the origin's defined marker and icon like any other, without erroring or treating it as unrecognized.
- The very first page of entries is itself empty. but the account is known to have entries further back (e.g., all of today's date-range filter would be empty for a date with none): paging continues to load older groups rather than showing the empty state, which is reserved for a true zero-entries account.
- A page load fails outright (not just going offline mid-session): the user sees a clear, retryable loading error for that page without losing or corrupting the entries already shown above it.
- The user reaches the end of their history: the list simply stops loading further pages without an error, with no "end of list" case to treat as a failure.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST provide a "Meus Registros" screen, reachable from the app's existing side-menu navigation, that fetches and displays all of the signed-in user's journal entries regardless of origin (manual, audio, photo, or chat).
- **FR-002**: Entries MUST be grouped under date headings by the calendar day they occurred ("Hoje" for today, "Ontem" for yesterday, an explicit date for anything older), with each entry rendered as a card showing: a marker and icon distinguishing its origin, its time, a text excerpt, any attached tags as read-only chips (only when present), and a per-entry synchronization badge.
- **FR-003**: The system MUST support browsing the user's complete entry history beyond what fits in a single fetch, loading further entries automatically as the user scrolls, and appending them without disturbing already-rendered cards or the user's current scroll position.
- **FR-004**: When the signed-in user has zero entries, the screen MUST show an empty state (illustration, "Nenhum registro ainda", and a "Criar primeiro registro" action) instead of an empty list; completing a save from that action MUST return the user to this screen with the new entry visible in its correct date group.
- **FR-005**: The per-entry synchronization badge MUST independently reflect exactly one of three states — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed for each entry from its own server-confirmed data together with the device's own knowledge of any write still pending or unreconciled for that entry, following the sync-badge semantics; this computation and its on-screen state MUST NOT depend on, be blocked by, or be delayed by session or authentication handling (login, silent renewal, or the expired-session overlay).
- **FR-006**: Loading or refreshing this screen's data MUST check the session and silently renew it when merely expired-but-renewable, without interrupting the user, consistent with the app's existing session-renewal behavior.
- **FR-007**: If the session cannot be silently renewed while this screen is open, the existing "Sessão expirada" overlay MUST appear on top of it without discarding the entries already loaded or the current scroll position; once the user re-authenticates, the overlay MUST dismiss and the screen MUST be restored exactly as it was. - **FR-008**: The screen's header download affordance and its search bar with funnel button MUST be rendered to match the prototype for visual fidelity, but MUST NOT perform export or search/filter behavior in this unit — those behaviors belong to later units and MUST NOT be implemented here.
- **FR-009**: While the device is offline, entries already loaded on this screen MUST remain visible and scrollable; attempting to load further pages MUST fail with a clear, retryable message rather than hanging or crashing, and no write of any kind MUST be attempted from this screen.

- **Journal Entry**: The same persisted, immutable record introduced by RF01 — text content, a creation/occurrence time, and an origin — now also carrying the server-confirmation data (its last-confirmed-write time and the ever-increasing revision counter) and any read-only tags attached to it, and now rendered regardless of which of the four possible origins (`manual`, `audio`, `photo`, `chat`) produced it.
- **Synchronization Badge State**: A derived, per-entry value — synchronized, synchronizing, or synchronization error — computed entirely on the device from an entry's own confirmation data and the device's own record of any write for that entry still pending or unreconciled; never itself stored by or requested directly from the backend.
- **Entry Timeline Page**: The windowed view of the user's full entry history currently loaded on screen — the entries fetched so far and the position to continue from — preserved across scrolling, backgrounding, and a session expiration/renewal cycle so the user's place is never lost.

- **SC-001**: 100% of a user's entries — across every origin they've used — appear exactly once in the timeline, correctly grouped by the day they occurred, with no entry requiring the user to know or remember which capture method created it.
- **SC-002**: 100% of accounts with zero entries see the empty state with a working path into creating their first entry, never a blank, broken, or perpetually-loading screen.
- **SC-003**: Users can scroll through their entire entry history, however long, with additional entries loading automatically in every case, without ever needing a manual "load more" action or losing their scroll position.
- **SC-004**: When a session expires while a user is viewing this screen, 100% of the time their loaded entries and scroll position are unchanged after they re-authenticate.
- **SC-005**: Every entry visible on screen shows one of the three defined synchronization states at all times, unaffected by whatever is happening with the user's session at that moment.

- Date-heading grouping ("Hoje", "Ontem", explicit dates) uses the device's local calendar day applied to each entry's occurrence timestamp, matching the prototype's labels.
- No entry-detail or full-text screen is introduced in this unit — see the resolved Clarification on `GET /entries/:id`'s purpose; a card's text excerpt is the only rendering of an entry's content here.
- "No BLoC imports another BLoC directly" (the requirement's own architecture-level acceptance criterion) is carried forward as an implementation-time constraint for the planning phase; at the specification level it is expressed through FR-005's and FR-007's independence requirements between the synchronization badge and session/authentication handling.
